subject: Post-call: Quantization tradeoffs & model-fit next steps (FinWave)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finwave.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — quantization tradeoffs / model fit

Thanks again for your time today, Elaine — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: run our recommendation & fraud-detection prompt set with low-tail latency <= 150ms and 95th percentile under 250ms for production inference.
- Top concern: avoid quality regressions when using aggressive quantization (AWQ/GPTQ) / FP8 tuning on your ensemble.
- Current footprint: 8M requests/day (burst to 12M), acceptance of batched inference if tail latency SLOs hold.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
1) Candidate models: rdx-mini-7B-finetuned (baseline), open-rw-13B-rlhf (higher-quality), rdx-8B-quant-safe (engineered for AWQ).
2) Eval plan: run our reference prompt set (attached prompt_set_v1.txt) + your top 50 customer queries. We’ll produce token-level diff metrics, embedding drift, and answer-level pass/fail for business-critical prompts.
3) Quantization trade study: baseline (FP16), pragmatic (GPTQ-4/8), aggressive (AWQ 4-bit) — we’ll report latency, memory, P50/P95, and a human-eval quality delta with examples.

Next steps (proposed):
- You: share the 50 sample queries + 2 representative user sessions (redacted) by end of week.
- Redwood (Michael/Dylan): run bench harness on the FinWave set, deliver instrumented results and the tradeoff slide deck by Thu next week (attached).
- Schedule follow-up: 30-min sync to review results — suggested Wed 24 Feb, 10:00am PT.

Attachments referenced: prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt set we used in call), quant_tradeoff_presentation.pdf (high-level tradeoffs & recommendation), finwave_benchmark_results.csv (we’ll populate after runs).

If that captures everything, I’ll book the follow-up.
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Park <elaine@finwave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinWave Platform Team <platform@finwave.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — quantization tradeoffs / model fit

Thanks Marissa — that looks right. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The top 50 queries will include many short-accounting-style prompts (very latency sensitive) and a smaller batch of longer, exploratory prompts. We care most about precision on the short prompts.
- On data sharing: we’ll redact PII but keep context. Expect the queries by Friday EOD.

Two asks before you run the heavy bench: 
1) Can Michael confirm which evaluation metrics you’ll report for "quality delta"? We need discrete pass/fail for compliance-sensitive prompts.
2) Is there a suggested safe starting point for quantization (e.g., GPTQ with per-channel vs per-tensor) so we don’t accidentally over-quantize in canary?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Engineering, FinWave
elaine@finwave.com

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finwave.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — quantization tradeoffs / model fit

Hi Elaine — quick answers and plan from the SE side: 

1) Quality metrics we will report (per-prompt and aggregate):
   - Discrete pass/fail (binary) for compliance-critical prompts you flag.
   - Rouge-L / BLEU-style overlap where applicable for structured outputs.
   - Semantic similarity (embedding cosine) for paraphrase-tolerance checks.
   - Human-rated quality delta on a 5-point scale for a 100-sample stratified set (we’ll include examples).
   - Error modes: hallucination rate, missing-entity rate, and format deviations.

2) Safe starting point for quantization:
   - Start with GPTQ 4-bit per-channel on rdx-8B-quant-safe and evaluate. Per-channel maintains better numeric fidelity for smaller matrices and tends to preserve quality on short prompts.
   - If tail latency requirements still aren’t met, try AWQ (4-bit) on a staging canary with a small percentage of traffic and compare human-eval deltas.
   - FP8 tuning is promising but higher risk for format-sensitive prompts; test FP8 on non-compliance traffic first.

3) Bench harness & outputs (what you’ll get):
   - finwave_benchmark_results.csv: token-level latencies (avg/P50/P95), memory footprint, throughput under configured batching.
   - quant_tradeoff_presentation.pdf: summary slides with recommended lane (conservative/pragmatic/aggressive) and rollout playbook.
   - Prompt-level diff examples and recommended fallback rules (e.g., route certain prompts to FP16 or higher-quality model variant).

Plan: We’ll run baseline (FP16) -> GPTQ-4 (per-channel) -> AWQ-4 -> FP8 (if feasible) across the three candidate models Marissa called out. We’ll tag runs with sample IDs and surface the top 10 fail cases for quick review. Expect results by Thu 25 Feb EOD.

Questions: can you confirm what % of traffic you’re comfortable routing to a canary for the AWQ stage? Typical customers start at 1–5% and step up based on QA signals.

Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0124

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finwave.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 17:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — quantization tradeoffs / model fit

Perfect, thanks Michael and Elaine. Elaine — 1–5% canary sounds good. If you’re okay I’ll book the Wed slot and Michael/Dylan will start the bench when your sample set arrives.

Action items recap: 
- Elaine: share 50 sample queries + 2 session traces (redacted) by Fri EOD (18 Feb).
- Michael/Dylan: run bench and deliver artifacts (CSV + deck + top 10 failures) by Thu 25 Feb EOD.
- Booking: follow-up 24 Feb, 10:00am PT (invite to follow).

Thanks team — speak soon.
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
